threads_text: US officials concluded that a Chinese businesswoman close to Jensen Huang was passing intelligence to Beijing, The New York Times reports. Officials believed Huang did not know, and Trump was briefed a year ago but did not act. Should chip CEOs be warned when spies get close to them?
caption:
A Chinese businesswoman with a close relationship to NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing, The New York Times reported.
She is Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data center company. US officials suspect Megaspeed helped China get NVIDIA chips.
A sister company bought at least $4.8 billion of AI hardware with NVIDIA chips from June 2024 to February 2026, per the report.
Officials believed Jensen Huang did not know. Trump was briefed about a year ago and did not act.
NVIDIA said meeting customers is part of a CEO's job. Megaspeed opened an internal investigation, and China's embassy called the claims "groundless smears and slanders."

Should tech CEOs get a warning when spies target them?
